lia (eng-platform): quick q — for the multi-variant canary we prototyped, should fallback be proactive at routing time (route-level soft-return) or purely reactive on metric triggers? cc @omar @tess
omar (eng-runtime): my 2c: proactive routing buys latency predictability but risks routing away useful capacity. reactive is simpler but can be noisier during bursts.
lia (eng-platform): yeah that's the trade. thinking about session affinity + variant-aware KV cache to reduce cold-start regressions.
tess (eng-ml): affinity + cache is nice for quality stability, but it complicates rollbacks. if we pin sessions to canary, we need a fast-unpin path to revert without orphaned cache entries.
ryan (eng-sre): fast-unpin should be a single atomic operation: mark session as unpinned and publish a TTL-zero marker so agents purge local KV shards. we did similar in nginx-layer failover.
kate (eng-runtime): agree. also we should differentiate fallback reasons: latency SLO breach vs model-quality regression. different actions: latency -> route to cheaper variant; quality -> serve previous stable model.
lia (eng-platform): proposal sketch below (short DSL). thoughts?
```
rollout "multi-variant-canary" {
  variants: [stable:v1, canary:v2, cheap:v2-quant]
  routing: {
    default: stable
    canary_percent: 10
    affinity: session
    fallback: {
      latency_threshold_ms: 1200 -> route: cheap
      quality_drop_pct: 3 -> route: stable
      sustained_5m: trigger_rollback
    }
  }
}
```
omar (eng-runtime): nice. call out that "cheap" variant may not be compatible for function-calling outputs; need capability labels on variants. router must check capability-match before fallback.
tess (eng-ml): and include a probabilistic hedging option for tail-latency spikes: duplicate 5% of requests to canary+cheap and pick fastest correct output. hedging can mask regressions though.
ryan (eng-sre): operations note: we need observable signals per session: last-known-variant, pinned-until, last-quality-sample. add to trace headers so we can investigate after incidents.
kate (eng-runtime): implementation-wise I think we can extend the routing table with a small state machine per session: {pinned, drifting, evicted}. transitions driven by timer + external signals. simple and testable.
lia (eng-platform): good. what about rollout pause criteria? we shouldn't just rely on a single quality metric. multi-signal: quality, latency, error-rate, and customer-impact tag.
omar (eng-runtime)::+1: multi-signal stop. Also: graceful fallback should attempt a bounded number of retries to alternative variant before failing fast to caller. keeps client experience consistent.
deploy-bot: deploy event: canary-config v2 applied to region-us-east at 2024-09-07T15:05:20Z
lia (eng-platform): thanks. next steps: 1) write an RFC for the route-level state machine and session unpin protocol; 2) telemetry contract for per-session signals; 3) a test harness that simulates bursty traffic + quality regressions. who volunteers to draft RFC?
omar (eng-runtime): I'll take the state machine draft.
tess (eng-ml): I'll drive the telemetry schema and evals integration.
ryan (eng-sre): I'll prototype the unpin purge mechanism and runbook entries.
kate (eng-runtime): I'll help with compatibility labels and router changes.
lia (eng-platform): awesome, assigning action items in the doc. if anyone thinks we missed a class of fallback (eg. cost-based preemption), flag it here.
tess (eng-ml): cost-based preemption is important for reserved GPU pools. maybe a routing policy that demotes expensive variants when budget usage > X%. fallback action = queue or route-to-cheap.
lia (eng-platform): noted. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
